clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 6423-A is the final approval, in the President's words 'Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Imported Date Packing Industry.' (the five numbered paragraphs before it are findings and command nothing). The order acts under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act and finds, among other things, that the code complies with the pertinent provisions of the Act including clauses (1) and (2) of subsection (a) of section 3, so the command is a section 3 approval whose operative effect depended on the code-approval provisions of Title I. No earlier end applies: the order states no period, condition or provisional approval, and no held record shows the code cancelled or suspended before June 14, 1935 (see earlier_end_check). The approval ended on June 14, 1935, when Congress approved S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375); its section 2 provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed'. The resolution states no effective date other than its approval and nothing defers section 2, so June 14, 1935 is the end of the prospective operative effect of the approval. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date; June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Actor: Congress, by S.J. Res. 113 section 2.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory lists only the five numbered findings and stops before the approval; the corrected span is the operative final paragraph, from 'Now, Therefore' through 'Imported Date Packing Industry.'

research_rationale:
EO 6423-A (signed November 11, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Imported Date Packing Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act after the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator each reported on it. The numbered paragraphs 1 to 5 are the President's findings, which command nothing; the one operative command is the final approval. Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list entry at p. 550 and the held text agree on number, date and subject. Source: the American Presidency Project transcription (a Common Crawl capture, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false); the page record with the same sha256 names this order's number, its date and subject agree with the text, and its text_sha256 is the held text's. The order is issued under Title I and does not delegate authority to the Secretary of Agriculture. The claim follows the reviewed shared analysis of NIRA code approvals: first end June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 section 2); Schechter recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date; accrued effects survive as past effects.

savings.reason: Nothing continues the approval after the repeal. Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code approved by this order before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, not continued operation of EO 6423-A. The section 5 antitrust exemption for action taken while the code was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for that past action; the resolution's proviso reads 'Provided, That the exemption provided in section 5 of such title shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder', names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle how far it narrowed the exemption for past action under codes. No held source shows a prosecution continued or any action under the code taken after June 14, 1935.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on the delegation ground and on the intrastate-commerce ground. It is recorded as a validity characterization of every section 3 code approval (void from issuance under the doctrine prevailing in 1935), not as an end of this order; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this approval.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of the National Industrial Recovery Act; not an end date
source_notes.reason: Section 3 of Title I states the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed by description: under 3(b) its provisions are the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under 3(c) the district courts may restrain violations, and under 3(f) a violation is a misdemeanor. Cited for the content of the repealed provisions, not for any date.
